excerpts.text: From 2021 to 2024, Australia’s population increased from 25.7 million to 27.2 million, reflecting a 5.9% increase. Net overseas migration contributed 1.17 million people (78% of total growth), with natural increase accounting for the remaining 335,000.

While capital cities experienced population growth of 1.17 million people (6.8%) compared to 336,000 (4.0%) in the rest of the country, there was a net outflow of more than 107,000 people leaving the cities to establish themselves in regional areas.

Following a similar pattern to other capital cities, growth was concentrated in the outskirts of the greater city area (due to internal migration and natural increase) and the inner city (due to overseas migration).
